classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied ordered congruence statement to match sides and angles, with triangle angle sums.

content.prompt: In each part, it is known that $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle DEF$. Determine the unknown angles and side lengths. (Side lengths are given correct to one decimal place.)

spec.description: Two separate triangles, ABC above DEF, with all original vertex, angle and side labels. Ordinary source-blue strokes are black under house style.
spec.mathematics: ABC corresponds to DEF. Given A=40 degrees, B=100 degrees, AC=4.6 cm, F=40 degrees, FE=ED=3.0 cm.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BCA&=180^\circ-40^\circ-100^\circ\\\angle BCA&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Matching angles give $\angle FED=\angle ABC=100^\circ$ and $\angle FDE=\angle BAC=40^\circ$.

Matching sides give $AB=DE=3.0\text{ cm}$, $BC=EF=3.0\text{ cm}$ and $FD=CA=4.6\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Paired separate triangles side by side. The 40-degree label belongs to A and the 130-degree label to C. Ordinary lines and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: Given AB=5.0 cm, A=40 degrees, C=130 degrees, FD=1.1 cm, FE=4.2 cm, D=40 degrees and E=10 degrees.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=180^\circ-40^\circ-130^\circ\\\angle ABC&=10^\circ\end{align*}$$
Matching angles give $\angle EFD=\angle BCA=130^\circ$.

Matching sides give $CB=FE=4.2\text{ cm}$, $AC=DF=1.1\text{ cm}$ and $ED=BA=5.0\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Two separate triangles side by side, retaining all original labels. Ordinary geometry is black.
spec.mathematics: B=32 degrees, BC=14.1 cm, F=37 degrees, D=111 degrees, FD=8.0 cm and DE=9.1 cm.

answer.short: $\angle FED=32^\circ$, $\angle CAB=111^\circ$, $\angle BCA=37^\circ$; $AB=9.1\text{ cm}$, $AC=8.0\text{ cm}$, $FE=14.1\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle FED&=180^\circ-37^\circ-111^\circ\\\angle FED&=32^\circ\end{align*}$$
Matching angles give $\angle CAB=\angle FDE=111^\circ$ and $\angle BCA=\angle EFD=37^\circ$.

Matching sides give $AB=DE=9.1\text{ cm}$, $AC=DF=8.0\text{ cm}$ and $FE=CB=14.1\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Two separate triangles side by side. All source givens remain, with black ordinary geometry.
spec.mathematics: AB=30.0 mm, F=46 degrees, D=67 degrees and FD=38.3 mm. The triangle DEF is isosceles after deriving E=67 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no derived equality marks.

answer.short: $\angle FED=67^\circ$, $\angle CAB=67^\circ$, $\angle ABC=67^\circ$, $\angle BCA=46^\circ$; $CB=AC=FE=38.3\text{ mm}$, $ED=30.0\text{ mm}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle FED&=180^\circ-46^\circ-67^\circ\\\angle FED&=67^\circ\end{align*}$$
Matching angles give $\angle CAB=67^\circ$, $\angle ABC=67^\circ$ and $\angle BCA=46^\circ$.

Since $\angle FED=\angle FDE$, the opposite sides are equal: $FE=FD=38.3\text{ mm}$.

Matching sides give $CB=FE=38.3\text{ mm}$, $AC=DF=38.3\text{ mm}$ and $ED=AB=30.0\text{ mm}$.
